title: Make durable citations packet- or content-specific

state.decision_rationale: Accepted and completed in MKTCTX/5: packet-local, packet-qualified, and full-content-qualified line and symbol citations have normative parsing, resolution, alias, rename, collision, and validation behavior.

provenance.review_target: Reported 396-file MKTCTX/3 packet; exact artifact not identified

feedback.verbatim: Version citations with the packet. F...:L12-L18 identifies a path and source lines, but those lines can change in another packet. The canonical durable citation should be closer to Pab781a4ee54f/Fc242cace9874:L12-L18 or include the content hash, such as Fc242cace9874@12ae50e4:L12-L18. The packet is already carrying everything required. Make the citation grammar explicit.
feedback.normalized_claim: Define an explicit citation grammar that binds path and line ranges to a particular packet or source-content identity.

current_behavior: The embedded guide defines file, symbol, and 1-based inclusive line handles but does not compose them with packet identity.
File IDs are path-derived and therefore survive content changes at the same path.
Packet ID is manifest-derived and source hashes bind file content, so both identity components needed for durable citations already exist.
No normative citation parser or citation-validation API exists.
evidence: src/context.ts: CONTEXT_GUIDE, stableFileId, packetId, and sourceHash

proposal.summary: Evaluate compact citation forms for packet-local navigation and durable cross-packet references, then specify their resolution and validation rules.
candidate_changes: Retain F...:Lx-Ly as an explicitly packet-local shorthand.
Define packet-qualified citations such as P.../F...:Lx-Ly for statements tied to a complete context snapshot.
Define content-qualified citations using a digest prefix when a source range should survive packet repackaging.
Specify symbol citations, alias resolution, digest-prefix collision behavior, and validation errors.
Add citation examples to the embedded guide only if the token cost materially improves model citation accuracy.
non_goals: Do not imply that path-derived file IDs bind a particular file version.
Do not treat line ranges as stable across content changes without a content or packet qualifier.
Do not create globally durable citations from truncated hashes without collision rules.

questions: Is packet identity or file-content identity the more useful default durability boundary?
How many digest characters are required, and where is collision uniqueness evaluated?
Should citations address exact source lines, chunks, symbols, or byte ranges?
How should alias paths cite canonical content while preserving the resource path that mattered to the claim?
risks: Long qualified citations consume tokens and reduce human readability.
Packet-qualified citations break when semantically identical context is re-rendered with a different manifest.
Content-qualified line citations can still become meaningless when copied content appears under a different language or path context.
Ambiguous digest prefixes can resolve differently across collections.
evidence_needed: Citation-resolution fixtures across repackaging, content edits, aliases, path renames, and digest-prefix collisions.
Blind model tests comparing packet-local and qualified citation accuracy.
Token-cost and readability comparison of candidate grammars.
A normative definition of citation resolution scope.
